title: 10. Exercises: Binary Search Tree Masterclass
summary: Exercises for Binary Search Tree Masterclass.
objectives: Solve the Binary Search Tree Masterclass exercises without looking at the lesson
Test edge cases and explain your approach

sections.title: What is a Tree? (Core Terminology) — Coding Challenges
sections.body:
```
CHALLENGE 1: Write a function to print all leaf nodes of a binary tree from left to right.

CHALLENGE 2: Given a binary tree, find the maximum depth (height) using an ITERATIVE 
             approach (no recursion). Use a queue.

CHALLENGE 3: Write a function that returns the number of nodes at each level of the tree 
             as a list. E.g., [1, 2, 3] means 1 node at level 0, 2 at level 1, 3 at level 2.

CHALLENGE 4: Given two nodes in a binary tree, find if they are at the same level.

CHALLENGE 5: Write a function to find the sum of all node values at a given depth D.

CHALLENGE 6: Given a binary tree, return True if it is a "full binary tree" 
             (every node has either 0 or 2 children, never 1).

CHALLENGE 7: Write a function to find the "width" of a binary tree — the maximum 
             number of nodes at any single level.
```

sections.title: What is a Binary Tree? — Coding Challenges
sections.body:
```
CHALLENGE 1: Write a function to check if a binary tree is a Perfect Binary Tree.
             (Hint: in a perfect tree, all leaves are at the same level)

CHALLENGE 2: Given a binary tree, return the mirror/inversion of the tree 
             WITHOUT modifying the original tree (create a new mirrored tree).

CHALLENGE 3: Write a function that converts a complete binary tree stored in 
             an array (heap representation) back into a linked node tree.
             Array: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
             
CHALLENGE 4: Given a binary tree, find the maximum width (max nodes at any level). 
             Return the level number AND the count.

CHALLENGE 5: Write a function to check if two binary trees are IDENTICAL 
             (same structure AND same values at every node).

CHALLENGE 6: Implement a function that converts a binary tree to its ZIGZAG 
             level-order representation (left-to-right, then right-to-left, alternating).

CHALLENGE 7: Given a binary tree, write a function to find the DIAMETER 
             (longest path between any two nodes — may not pass through root).
```

sections.title: What is a Binary Search Tree (BST)? — Coding Challenges
sections.body:
```
CHALLENGE 1: Write a function that takes a sorted array and builds a BALANCED BST from it.
             The root should be the middle element.
             Input:  [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
             Output: BST with 4 as root, height = 2

CHALLENGE 2: Given a BST, convert it to a sorted array WITHOUT using any extra 
             data structure (modify the tree itself to extract sorted values).

CHALLENGE 3: Write a function to find the SECOND LARGEST element in a BST in O(h) 
             time where h is the height of the tree.

CHALLENGE 4: Given a BST with string values, write a function to find all words 
             that come alphabetically between two given words (inclusive).
             Input: BST of words, word1="cat", word2="dog"
             Output: All words >= "cat" and <= "dog"

CHALLENGE 5: Write a function to count how many nodes in a BST fall within 
             a given range [low, high].

CHALLENGE 6: Given two BSTs, write a function to check if they contain the 
             same set of values (regardless of structure).

CHALLENGE 7: Write a function that, given a BST and a target value K, returns 
             True if there exist TWO nodes in the BST whose values sum to K.
             Achieve this without using any extra data structure.
```

sections.title: BST Node Structure in Python — Coding Challenges
sections.body:
```
CHALLENGE 1: Implement a BST node that uses Python's comparison operators (__lt__, __gt__, 
             __eq__) so that nodes can be compared directly with <, >, == operators.

CHALLENGE 2: Write a function that takes a BST and returns its representation as a 
             dictionary where keys are values and values are {'left': x, 'right': y}.

CHALLENGE 3: Implement a BST node that is "hashable" (can be put in a Python set or 
             used as a dict key) while still being mutable.

CHALLENGE 4: Create a BST implementation that uses Python's __getitem__ and __setitem__ 
             so you can do: bst[50] = "fifty" and print(bst[50]).

CHALLENGE 5: Write a deepcopy function for a BST WITHOUT using Python's copy module.
             The function should create a completely independent copy of the entire tree.

CHALLENGE 6: Implement a BST node that tracks HOW MANY TIMES each value was accessed 
             (searched for), and add a method to return the top 3 most accessed values.

CHALLENGE 7: Design a BST where each node stores a list of values (not just one), 
             and the BST ordering is based on the MINIMUM value in each list.
```
